recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It completes the explicit Medication Module guidance from FHIR-34293 without reintroducing bidirectional resource elements and aligns with FHIR-39018.
issue_request: FHIR-34293 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for R5. It requested removal of MedicationRequest.detectedIssue because DetectedIssue already points to implicated therapies and FHIR should avoid bidirectional links; the resolution also said to remove the element from MedicationDispense and add Medication Module guidance for accessing associated detected issues.
initial_application: Commit 26e2a82259 removed MedicationRequest.detectedIssue and MedicationDispense.detectedIssue from the StructureDefinitions and removed example references from MedicationRequest and MedicationDispense examples. Current source still has no direct MedicationRequest.detectedIssue or MedicationDispense.detectedIssue element, but that historical commit did not update source/medications-module.html.
additional_context: MedicationRequest and MedicationDispense are active current-build resources and source/medications-module.html is the active Medications module page. DetectedIssue.implicated and the DetectedIssue-implicated search parameter already define the reverse association. Later FHIR-39018 resolved Not Persuasive and confirmed that FHIR references are not bidirectional and that the DetectedIssue search parameter is the retrieval path.
reconciliation: Added one Common Use Cases bullet to source/medications-module.html explaining that MedicationRequest and MedicationDispense do not point directly to DetectedIssue, that DetectedIssue.implicated carries the association, and that clients can use direct DetectedIssue?implicated searches or _revinclude=DetectedIssue:implicated. The guidance also preserves containment when the issue has no independent lifecycle and need not be searched directly.
source_changes: source/medications-module.html: added a Common Use Cases bullet explaining retrieval of medication-related DetectedIssue instances through DetectedIssue.implicated, direct DetectedIssue?implicated searches, _revinclude=DetectedIssue:implicated, and containment when direct search is unnecessary.

related_jiras.note: Later R5 ballot request to keep MedicationRequest.detectedIssue was resolved Not Persuasive and confirmed the DetectedIssue.implicated/search-parameter approach.
Earlier STU3 guidance request explained why the former MedicationRequest/MedicationDispense detectedIssue references needed implementer guidance before FHIR-34293 removed the direct elements.
